+# tasks-axi project config — copy to `.tasks.toml` in the repo that owns the backlog.
+#
+# ── THE DELIVERY SWITCH ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# `backend` is the ONE line that decides where tasks live. It ships as
+# "markdown" on purpose: everything below is prepared so flipping it to "ado"
+# is a one-word, one-line change — and that flip is a deliberate Captain step,
+# not something a setup command or a default does for you.
+#
+# Before flipping, dry-run the exact production code path without switching:
+#
+#     tasks-axi list --backend ado
+#     tasks-axi show <some-id> --backend ado --full
+#
+# `--backend` overrides this file for one command. A green read proves the org,
+# project, area, credential, and join field; meta/followup fields wait for a write.
+backend = "markdown"
+# backend = "ado"   # ← Captain-only: flip when the ADO project is provisioned
+
+[markdown]
+path = "data/backlog.md"
+archive = "data/done-archive.md"
+done_keep = 10
+
+# ── Azure DevOps backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Read whenever `backend = "ado"` (or `--backend ado` / TASKS_AXI_BACKEND=ado).
+# Present here without being active: resolving this table has no side effects.
+[ado]
+org = "contoso"
+project = "Internal"
+# Root area path new work items land in; also scopes every read (WIQL `UNDER`),
+# so tasks-axi never sees unrelated work items in the project.
+# Single quotes: an area path contains backslashes, and tasks-axi refuses
+# doubled separators from TOML or the environment rather than guessing.
+area = 'Internal\Firstmate\main'
+
+# The join key and the tasks-axi residue. All three must exist as custom fields
+# on the work item type below BEFORE the switch. id_field must be a String field
+# for WIQL equality; meta_field and followup_field must be PlainText (long-text)
+# fields because ADO String fields are limited to 255 characters and can reject
+# or truncate their payloads. A missing id_field fails the dry read; missing
+# meta_field fails an ordinary create or update, while missing followup_field
+# fails a public-followup operation. Only this work item type is managed.
+work_item_type = "Task"
+id_field = "Custom.TasksAxiId"
+meta_field = "Custom.TasksAxiMeta"
+followup_field = "Custom.TasksAxiPublicFollowup"
+
+# ADO state names per tasks-axi state; the FIRST entry is what writes use, the
+# rest are accepted on read. These defaults write Agile-process Task states;
+# Scrum and Basic task workflows need explicit mappings before the switch.
+# A dry read cannot prove write states; a wrong first entry fails on the first
+# create or transition and names the rejected state.
+state_queued = "New, To Do, Proposed"
+state_in_flight = "Active, In Progress, Doing, Committed"
+state_done = "Closed, Done, Resolved, Removed"

235	```toml
   236	# .tasks.toml in the project root
   237	backend = "markdown"
   238	
   239	[markdown]
   240	path = "data/backlog.md"
   241	archive = "data/done-archive.md"
   242	done_keep = 10
   243	```
   244	
   245	`archive` is optional; when omitted, pruned tasks are appended to `done-archive.md` next to the active backlog.
   246	Body replacements with `--archive-body` append superseded bodies to `note-archive.md` next to the active backlog.
   247	
   248	## Backends
   249	
   250	Backends live behind a narrow `Store` interface, so the CLI layer never knows which one is active.
   251	
   252	| Backend                | Status            |
   253	| ---------------------- | ----------------- |
   254	| markdown               | shipped           |
   255	| ado (Azure DevOps)     | shipped (phase 1) |
   256	| sqlite                 | planned           |
   257	| github / jira / linear | planned           |
   258	
   259	### Azure DevOps
   260	
   261	```toml
   262	backend = "ado"
   263	
   264	[ado]
   265	org = "contoso"
   266	project = "Internal"
   267	area = 'Internal\Firstmate\main'    # optional: scope + where new work items land
   268	# work_item_type  = "Task"
   269	# id_field        = "Custom.TasksAxiId"
   270	# meta_field      = "Custom.TasksAxiMeta"
   271	# followup_field  = "Custom.TasksAxiPublicFollowup"
   272	# state_queued    = "New, To Do"        # first entry is the value tasks-axi writes
   273	# state_in_flight = "Active, In Progress"
   274	# state_done      = "Closed, Done"
   275	```
   276	
   277	Note the **single quotes** on `area`: an ADO area path contains backslashes, and tasks-axi rejects doubled separators from TOML or `TASKS_AXI_ADO_AREA` rather than silently targeting the wrong area.
   278	
   279	`org` / `project` / `area` also read `TASKS_AXI_ADO_ORG` / `_PROJECT` / `_AREA`.
   280	Auth is a PAT from `TASKS_AXI_ADO_PAT` (or `ADO_PAT` / `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT` / `AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT`), falling back to `az account get-access-token`.
   281	The PAT needs **Work Items (read & write)**. Azure DevOps answers an unauthenticated REST call with `203` and an HTML sign-in page rather than a `401`, so tasks-axi detects that shape and reports it as a rejected credential.
   282	
   283	#### Switching a live backlog onto ADO
   284	
   285	`backend` is the one line that decides where tasks live, and nothing flips it for you — no default, no `setup` command.
   286	Changing it does not migrate data: an empty ADO scope appears as an empty backlog, and existing Markdown tasks stop being visible to the CLI. Seed the ADO items and verify a known task with `tasks-axi show <id> --backend ado --full` before switching.
   287	Before flipping it, dry-run the exact production code path without switching:
   288	
   289	```sh
   290	tasks-axi list --backend ado          # reads from ADO, changes no config
   291	tasks-axi show <id> --backend ado --full
   292	```
   293	
   294	`--backend` overrides the config file for a single command, so a green read proves the org, project, area, credential, and join field; `meta_field` is exercised by an ordinary create or update, while `followup_field` is exercised only by a public-followup operation.
   295	See [`.tasks.toml.example`](.tasks.toml.example) for a fully prepared table with the switch left off.
   296	The three custom fields (`id_field`, `meta_field`, `followup_field`) must exist on the work item type **before** the switch. Configure `id_field` as a String field for WIQL equality, and configure `meta_field` and `followup_field` as PlainText (long-text) fields; ADO String fields are limited to 255 characters and can reject or truncate their payloads. A missing `id_field` fails the dry-read WIQL request, a missing `meta_field` fails an ordinary create or update, and a missing `followup_field` fails a public-followup operation. Only items of the configured `work_item_type` are managed.
   297	
   298	The default state map writes the Azure DevOps Agile-process Task states `New`, `Active`, and `Closed`. Scrum and Basic task workflows need explicit state mappings before the switch; a dry read cannot prove write states, so an incorrect mapping fails on the first create or transition and names the rejected state.
   299	Adds targeting In flight or Done create the work item in the queued state and then apply the ordinary optimistic transition; if the transition reports an error, its outcome is unconfirmed, so retry `start` or `done` idempotently. A requested close date remains pending until a successful `done` transition consumes it. If an item is reopened and completed again entirely in ADO between tasks-axi reads, tasks-axi continues to report its previously recorded close date.
   300	The three tasks-axi states map 1:1 onto `System.State`, bodies are HTML-encoded in `System.Description` and decoded on read so Boards renders their text literally, dependencies are work item links, and the public-followup obligation lives in its own field with the same canonical payload the markdown backend writes.
   301	Parent and discovered-from links are imported only when marked as tasks-axi-owned; ordinary native ADO hierarchy links are ignored.
   302	ADO reads also fail closed when a public-followup work item's title, body, or links drift from its public-safe promise through an out-of-band Boards edit. Applying the same strictness to hand-edited Markdown backlogs is a separate compatibility decision.
   303	`AdoStore.moveTo(id, areaPath)` implements cross-queue moves as Area Path changes, but refuses to move connected tasks outside the configured area; wiring safe area-path moves into the still markdown/path-shaped CLI `mv` verb is a follow-up.
   304	The ADO backend has no `prune`, `render`, archive-body, or CLI move support. `rm` checks active dependents from a best-effort snapshot, but ADO has no cross-item transaction or DELETE revision precondition, so a concurrent dependency can race that check; removal is unconditional but recoverable from the recycle bin. Public-followup delivery has the same containment: blocker state is checked before the obligation's revision-guarded patch, so a concurrent blocker reopen can race delivery advancement.
   305	
   306	## Development
   307	
   308	```sh
   309	pnpm install
   310	pnpm build         # tsc -> dist/
   311	pnpm test          # vitest
   312	pnpm lint          # eslint
   313	pnpm run build:skill -- --check   # fail if the generated skill is stale
   314	```
   315	
   316	The installable skill is generated from the same description and help the CLI prints, so it can never drift.
   317	
   318	## Contributing
   319	
   320	Contributions are welcome.
   321	Human-authored PRs targeting `main` are raised through the [`no-mistakes`](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes) gate, which runs review/test/lint/CI before opening the PR.
   322	See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full workflow and repo conventions.

    45	author: ${SKILL_AUTHOR}
    46	metadata:

    51	
    52	# tasks-axi
    53	
    54	${DESCRIPTION}
    55	
    56	You do not need tasks-axi installed globally - invoke it with \`npx -y tasks-axi <command>\`.
    57	If tasks-axi output shows a follow-up command starting with \`tasks-axi\`, run it as \`npx -y tasks-axi ...\` instead.
    58	
    59	tasks-axi stores tasks in the configured backend. Markdown is the default and uses a hand-editable \`backlog.md\` with a byte-exact round-trip. Archive-body, prune, render, and CLI move are Markdown-only and unavailable with ADO.
    60	
    61	## When to use
    62	
    63	Use tasks-axi whenever a task touches the backlog: filing or dispatching work, moving a task through queued -> in flight -> done, recording a PR url or report path on completion, tracking blocked-by dependencies, pausing dispatch with structured holds, finding dispatchable ready work or intentionally held work, or trimming the Done list.
    64	
    65	## Workflow
    66	
    67	1. Run \`npx -y tasks-axi\` with no arguments for a dashboard of the current backlog - in flight work, queued work with blockers, and suggested next commands.
    68	2. Drill in verb-first: \`list\`, \`show <id>\`, \`ready\`, then mutate with \`add\`, \`start\`, \`done\`, \`block\`/\`unblock\`, \`hold\`/\`unhold\`, \`update\`.
    69	3. The long notes never appear in \`list\`; run \`show <id> --full\` to read a task's complete body before replacing it.

    72	6. \`hold <id> --reason "<text>"\` pauses dispatch without prose parsing; \`ready\` excludes active holds by default, and \`ready --include-held\` shows a separate held group.
    73	   Use \`--until YYYY-MM-DD\` for a date gate that becomes inactive on and after that date.
    74	7. Human-readable responses include contextual next-step hints under \`help:\` when there is a useful follow-up - follow them.

    85	## Tips
    86	
    87	- Output is TOON-encoded and token-efficient; the long task body is truncated by default - the whole point is that \`list\` stays cheap.
    88	  Use \`--full\` only when you need the complete notes.
    89	- Every write leads with an \`ok:\` line confirming the write result, including the resulting task state when the command changes one (e.g. \`ok: start <id> -> In flight\`, \`ok: done <id> -> Done (pr <url>)\`, \`ok: render -> normalized <n>\`), then state-aware next-step hints.

   246	Body replacements with `--archive-body` append superseded bodies to `note-archive.md` next to the active backlog.
   247	
   248	## Backends
   249	
   250	Backends live behind a narrow `Store` interface, so the CLI layer never knows which one is active.
   251	
   252	| Backend                | Status            |
   253	| ---------------------- | ----------------- |
   254	| markdown               | shipped           |
   255	| ado (Azure DevOps)     | shipped (phase 1) |
   256	| sqlite                 | planned           |
   257	| github / jira / linear | planned           |
   258	
   259	### Azure DevOps
   260	
   261	```toml
   262	backend = "ado"
   263	
   264	[ado]
   265	org = "contoso"
   266	project = "Internal"
   267	area = 'Internal\Firstmate\main'    # optional: scope + where new work items land
   268	# work_item_type  = "Task"
   269	# id_field        = "Custom.TasksAxiId"
   270	# meta_field      = "Custom.TasksAxiMeta"
   271	# followup_field  = "Custom.TasksAxiPublicFollowup"
   272	# state_queued    = "New, To Do"        # first entry is the value tasks-axi writes
   273	# state_in_flight = "Active, In Progress"
   274	# state_done      = "Closed, Done"
   275	```
   276	
   277	Note the **single quotes** on `area`: an ADO area path contains backslashes, and tasks-axi rejects doubled separators from TOML or `TASKS_AXI_ADO_AREA` rather than silently targeting the wrong area.
   278	
   279	`org` / `project` / `area` also read `TASKS_AXI_ADO_ORG` / `_PROJECT` / `_AREA`.
   280	Auth is a PAT from `TASKS_AXI_ADO_PAT` (or `ADO_PAT` / `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT` / `AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT`), falling back to `az account get-access-token`.
   281	The PAT needs **Work Items (read & write)**. Azure DevOps answers an unauthenticated REST call with `203` and an HTML sign-in page rather than a `401`, so tasks-axi detects that shape and reports it as a rejected credential.
   282	
   283	#### Switching a live backlog onto ADO
   284	
   285	`backend` is the one line that decides where tasks live, and nothing flips it for you — no default, no `setup` command.
   286	Changing it does not migrate data: an empty ADO scope appears as an empty backlog, and existing Markdown tasks stop being visible to the CLI. Seed the ADO items and verify a known task with `tasks-axi show <id> --backend ado --full` before switching.
   287	Before flipping it, dry-run the exact production code path without switching:
   288	
   289	```sh
   290	tasks-axi list --backend ado          # reads from ADO, changes no config
   291	tasks-axi show <id> --backend ado --full
   292	```
   293	
   294	`--backend` overrides the config file for a single command, so a green read proves the org, project, area, credential, and join field; `meta_field` is exercised by an ordinary create or update, while `followup_field` is exercised only by a public-followup operation.
   295	See [`.tasks.toml.example`](.tasks.toml.example) for a fully prepared table with the switch left off.
   296	The three custom fields (`id_field`, `meta_field`, `followup_field`) must exist on the work item type **before** the switch. Configure `id_field` as a String field for WIQL equality, and configure `meta_field` and `followup_field` as PlainText (long-text) fields; ADO String fields are limited to 255 characters and can reject or truncate their payloads. A missing `id_field` fails the dry-read WIQL request, a missing `meta_field` fails an ordinary create or update, and a missing `followup_field` fails a public-followup operation. Only items of the configured `work_item_type` are managed.
   297	
   298	The default state map writes the Azure DevOps Agile-process Task states `New`, `Active`, and `Closed`. Scrum and Basic task workflows need explicit state mappings before the switch; a dry read cannot prove write states, so an incorrect mapping fails on the first create or transition and names the rejected state.
   299	Adds targeting In flight or Done create the work item in the queued state and then apply the ordinary optimistic transition; if the transition reports an error, its outcome is unconfirmed, so retry `start` or `done` idempotently. A requested close date remains pending until a successful `done` transition consumes it. If an item is reopened and completed again entirely in ADO between tasks-axi reads, tasks-axi continues to report its previously recorded close date.
   300	The three tasks-axi states map 1:1 onto `System.State`, bodies are HTML-encoded in `System.Description` and decoded on read so Boards renders their text literally, dependencies are work item links, and the public-followup obligation lives in its own field with the same canonical payload the markdown backend writes.
   301	Parent and discovered-from links are imported only when marked as tasks-axi-owned; ordinary native ADO hierarchy links are ignored.
   302	ADO reads also fail closed when a public-followup work item's title, body, or links drift from its public-safe promise through an out-of-band Boards edit. Applying the same strictness to hand-edited Markdown backlogs is a separate compatibility decision.
   303	`AdoStore.moveTo(id, areaPath)` implements cross-queue moves as Area Path changes, but refuses to move connected tasks outside the configured area; wiring safe area-path moves into the still markdown/path-shaped CLI `mv` verb is a follow-up.
   304	The ADO backend has no `prune`, `render`, archive-body, or CLI move support. `rm` checks active dependents from a best-effort snapshot, but ADO has no cross-item transaction or DELETE revision precondition, so a concurrent dependency can race that check; removal is unconditional but recoverable from the recycle bin.    308	```sh
   309	pnpm install
   310	pnpm build         # tsc -> dist/
   311	pnpm test          # vitest
   312	pnpm lint          # eslint
   313	pnpm run build:skill -- --check   # fail if the generated skill is stale
   314	```
